domain_rationale: Correctness is decided by an ocean carrier's import demurrage and detention tariff: how container moves (discharge, gate-out full, empty return) become terminal and merchant stages, how free time is counted in working days and around terminal closures, how tiered per-diem scales and their dated revisions price chargeable days, and how a contract discount is taken on an invoice run at a cut-off. The deliverable is the carrier's container charge statement, a logistics billing artifact; the code is the medium, not the subject, so Software would misplace it, and the judgement is freight-operations practice rather than finance or regulatory compliance.
evidence: instruction.md: symptoms are consignee disputes over container charges (free time over weekends, holidays and a terminal closure, stay counts, top-tier billing, rate revision timing, discounts)

environment/app/docs/tariff-rules.md: a numbered carrier tariff (stages, working-day free time, closures, chargeable days, revisions in force, non-retroactive tiers, accruals versus charges, discount)

planned verifier (step 4 onward): whole-statement comparison of every container's stage figures, amounts, discount and net, and the invoice total, against expectations sealed from solution/model.py, which is derived from the tariff
task.toml: category Operations, subcategory Logistics, tags logistics / ocean-shipping / demurrage-and-detention
